I bought this headset primarily for video conferencing with my teams now that I primarily work from home. I alternated between either my AirPods or Bose QC35's for a while and while they worked well for short calls, the batteries would die quickly or they would begin to hurt my ears. The Razer headsets were highly recommended by a coworker who does a lot of gaming so I gave them a shot.

The Good:
For the price, these are an amazing wired headset. They are extremely light as advertised and after a while of wearing them, you don't notice them on your head. They feel very well constructed and don't feel like cheap plastic headphones. The ear cups are quite large and deep and do not press on your ear. They have lots of padding to make them comfortable for long periods of time. The microphone is extremely clear. People on calls have been impressed with how clear my voice sounds with almost no background noise being heard. It comes with a decent length 3.5mm Stereo/Mic jack and a longer extension cable to split the audio out and microphone in, which is a nice addition for some users.

The Not-So-Good:
- The headphone's audio is good, but it's not great out of the box. Razer advertises this headset as a 7.1 Surround Sound headset but their 7.1 Surround Sound software is only available on Windows, which was a bit of a let down as a Mac user. I ended up installing Boom3D on my Mac which I assume is doing a similar thing as their software, and it sounds better.

- There is not a ton of padding at the top of the headphones which can hurt the top of your head after long periods of time. (though this seems to be the case with most over-ear headsets).

- Razer advertises this headset with "Eyewear Channels" for comfort while wearing glasses, but I have found that after long periods of time with glasses the sides of your head can hurt a bit.

I highly recommend this headset for people wanting a solid multi-use headset without dealing with the hassle of batteries, Bluetooth, and high costs.

example_docs: I don't know if it works, because my ds died, but it did came well packed for a cable and it seemed sturdy enough. The only problem maybe was lenght.

Technical Stuff - Integrated Graphics - Audio "Unplugged" issueS:

I ordered this, intending to put it on my media center PC connected via HDMI to my living room TV. I had read about some audio latency issues so I connected a subwoofer and speakers to the PC via audio jack to avoid that particular issue. My concern after that was that I am running a sandy bridge core i3, 2120T. Basically a 2.5ghz Sandy with integrated graphics. After reading some of the reviews here I was worried about game performance. I wasn't overly worried because I do have a low profile Geforce 520 I could stick in the machine if the CPU/GPU couldn't handle the game, I just didn't want to do that unless I had to because I want to keep the power consumption, heat, and fan noise to a minimum in my living room pc. The game arrived yesterday and after the lengthy install process, I fired it up, only to find that during the setup, it kept saying the cable was unplugged. I was quite frustrated reading forums and finding that people had been getting bogus cables and had to have new ones sent. I did, however, read on one forum that audio management programs running in the system tray can sometimes interfere. I ended task on my realtek audio manager but this did not resolve the problem. I realized that it might be the audio component of my hauppauge dual tuner, so I disabled that device in device manager. The PC asked for a restart - but I did not restart it - and Rocksmith worked like a champ. After I was done playing I just re-enabled my tuner, and again, declined to restart the PC. A minor annoyance but it definitely is a solid work around and I would encourage others to try this before sending out for a new cable. The next thing that was a pleasant surprise was the graphics, latency, performance, other issues people were talking about - non existent for me. The game plays great. If you can't get it to run on Sandy Bridge or Ivy Bridge integrated graphics, you better take a look at your machine because you have other problems. The machine I run it on has the i3-2120T, 8GB DDR3, Sandy Bridge HD2000 graphics, and a 7200RPM Platter drive on Windows 7 Home Premium 64 Bit. So mostly I am writing this review to let people know that if they are on the fence about getting this for a machine with lower end graphics, to encourage them to give it a try, and also to let people know that there are work arounds to get the cable to work if you get the dreaded "unplugged" error.

Gameplay:

The game itself has been really fun. I have been playing for about 3 years, from books and videos, by myself. I wouldn't consider myself anything more than an amateur hobbyist. I am having fun with the events, and with the technique training. Some of it is frustrating - I would much rather have a tab notation than the current format of "guitar-hero-like" colored notes dropping toward the string. Give me a scrolling TAB option - because that's how I'm used to playing. But then, I have maybe 2 hours total playtime on it so far - I'm sure I'll get used to it over time, and hey - I'm already addicted.

Enjoy!

Update:

Played at lunchtime today and didn't bother disabling the hauppauge card. It worked without having to use my workaround. Maybe it only needed that done the first time through? Unsure but everything works smoothly now without having to do anything extra. Happy camper!

Update 2:

Also plays perfectly fine on my laptop with i5-3317u, 4gb ram, and intel cpu integrated graphics.
Also should note that I have gone from 15-20 minutes of practice time a day to 1 or 2 hours thanks to Rocksmith. It makes it so much more fun!

example_docs: I like Trevor Noah as a comedian and generally likable guy. This book falls into the trap of the first novel. It contains biographical stories. I did enjoy the first five stories tremendously. He does begin to get repetitious with certain themes, mostly Apartheid, which the reader already knows is horrible. He drives in this point story after story. Besides that, he is a gifted and brilliant writer, and the stories are so poignant. I loved most of them. However, I am not even halfway through, and not looking forward to more heavy handed stories about how horrible apartheid is, which I already knew. While not entirely what I expected, the game proved to be 100% south park every single minute, and many times felt like watching an episode despite its interactive nature. The fighting mechanics take a bit of getting used to, but the gameplay is solid and what bugs I've encountered were minor. That said, having completed the game it left me wanting more, hoping for DLC's, and regretting the content that got cut. In a nutshell, here's some pros and cons that sum things up:

+ Definitive South Park Look, Feel and Humor
+ Extensive game play mechanics
+ Plenty of side quests, options, and classes add replay value
+ Multiple references to items and situations throughout the series
+ Experience the familiar places, characters, and attitude of South Park first hand!
+ The possibility of DLC expansion beyond costume sets
+ Works with Keyboard+Mouse, XBox 360 Controller for Windows, or PS3 Controller using Motioninjoy
+ Interfaces with Steam allowing you to play on any machine

- Frustrating Tutorials at times throughout the game due to faulty explanations of commands
- Minor bugs that are trivial but can frustrate (such as walking out the door instead of looting a chest)
- Relatively Short, perhaps 15-20 hours
- Humor not appropriate for children
- Cut content leaves player wanting more

Overall, if you're a South Park fan, I'd highly recommend, but if you don't care for South Park it would be hard to justify the purchase, as there are plenty of other games with similar mechanics that don't involve anal probes, fart jokes and the like.
